author: Bryan Shin
title: Netflix Raises Subscription Price
text:
01/15/2019 93
Netflix, Inc. (NASDAQ: NFLX) raised its subscription prices again, which sent shares rising by 6% shortly after the opening bell on Tuesday, according to the Wall Street Journal .
Netflix’s cheapest basic plan will increase from USD 8 to USD 9, the standard plan will jump from USD 11 to USD 13, and the 4K Premium plan will go up from USD 14 to USD 16.
The increased pricing plan represents a 13% to 18% hike, which is the Company’s biggest increase since launching its streaming service 12 years ago, according to CNBC .
The new pricing plan will take effect immediately for new customers. Existing customers will see their price plans change on their bills over the next several months.
“We change pricing from time to time as we continue investing in great entertainment and improving the overall Netflix experience for the benefit of our members,” a Netflix spokesperson said.
Netflix previously increased its price plan back in October 2017, which sent shares rising by 4% then. The previous price hike then did not seem to concern investors. In return, Netflix delivered strong quarterly results which sent shares on a year-long bullish run.
The extra cash generated from the hiked plans will help Netflix’s investment in its original shows and films as well as help finance debt competing against other companies entering the streaming industry such as Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), Disney (NYSE: DIS), and Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL).
Netflix is the best performing stock among FAANG. Netflix’s stock price has increased by 31.9% since starting the new year. Amazon follows behind Netflix, increasing only 9.6% this year so far.
Separately, Goldman Sachs analysts project strong quarterly earnings from Netflix when it reports on Thursday. The firm projects a 20% upside for the Company’s stock, according to CNBC .
